cap: Pattern recognition does most of the work on transvaginal ultrasound. Fluid is anechoic and a simple cyst needs only a repeat scan; lace-like echoes with a retracting clot mean a hemorrhagic cyst, uniform ground-glass echoes an endometrioma, and a bright Rokitansky nodule with a shadow a dermoid. An enlarged ovary with follicles at its edge and a whirlpool sign of the twisted pedicle means torsion.
teach: Name the pattern first, then act on it. Simple, hemorrhagic and endometrioma patterns in a premenopausal woman are watched with a repeat scan unless they hurt or grow; a dermoid is removed by cystectomy when it is large or symptomatic because its weight invites torsion; torsion is surgical at once, and normal Doppler flow does not exclude it because the artery is the last vessel to close.
